answer: First, verifiers broadcast a nebula seed to prospective agents. Each agent immediately walks sequential cache-line hops across 64 GB of pseudo-random RAM within strict 50-nanosecond budgets, chasing pointers like footsteps through a dark forest. The agent seals traversed offsets using an internal cipher into a cedar cryptographic proof. Verifiers audit round-trip timing; stalled responses or corrupted seals immediately purge identity status and slash deposits. Emulating 1,000 concurrent agents demands 64 TB of dedicated memory costing $28,000 monthly.
